title: THE HEART THAT WOULD NOT TAKE IT TO HEART

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Instead, he turned and went into his palace, and did not take even this to heart. And all the Egyptians dug along the Nile to get drinking water, because they could not drink the water of the river. Seven days passed after the Lord struck the Nile." - Exodus 7:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
That is one of the saddest sentences in Exodus: he did not take even this to heart. He simply turned, walked into his palace, and shut the door.

Meanwhile his people were on their knees in the mud, digging along the riverbank for water. Pharaoh had a palace and servants. His stubbornness cost the ordinary people far more than it cost him.

Then comes the last line: seven days passed. A full week of undrinkable water, and still nothing changed in Pharaoh's heart.

The phrase to take to heart is the crucial one. Many of us receive warnings and simply do not take them to heart. A health scare, a strained relationship, a nagging conviction after a sermon — we notice it, we turn, and we walk into our own palace.

God is patient, but time is not unlimited. Paul writes that now is the day of salvation (2 Cor 6:2). Take it to heart today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God shown me recently that I noticed but did not take to heart?
2. Whose life is affected by my refusal to change?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, do not let me walk away from what You are showing me. Give me a heart that takes Your word seriously today. Amen.
